packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — packet 13

Inputs limited to this packet's prompt, metadata and two images. No catalogue, edition, prior transcription or proposed identification consulted or exposed.

Layout survey
Both images are upright. A central fold divides each broad fragment into two page-like areas, each bearing one broad text column. Brown writing is accompanied by red paragraph marks and red underlining. Image-002 is markedly clearer than image-001. There are no secure running titles. The red lines underline both short phrases and longer multi-line stretches; these plausibly distinguish quotation/lemma from surrounding prose, but that textual function remains an interpretation. Paragraph openings sometimes have enlarged or red-touched capitals. Occasional marginal marks and extensions occur, but no independent dense marginal commentary is evident. No interlinear gloss securely recognized. The photographs appear to show opposite faces of the same fragment, not duplicate text crops.

Selection and line convention
Selected image-002's upper-left red-underlined passage and the lower-right paragraph introduced by a red-touched capital. L and R indicate the two columns/page areas, with physical lines counted from their first written baseline at the top of the ORIGINAL image. The line number refers to a whole physical line even when part is unread. Proposed expansions are parenthesized; question marks retain doubt.

Sample A — image-002.jpg, upper left
Surrounding prose:
image-002.jpg L1: quid hic caritas mirabilis? De qua d(icitu)r?
image-002.jpg L2: [illegible] O inestimabilis dilectio ca
image-002.jpg L3: ritatis ut seruū redimeret filiū tradidisti hic
image-002.jpg L4: mirabilem? mutacione(m) [illegible] fontē olei [hole] [illegible]
image-002.jpg L5: in [deleted/overwritten word, illegible] hora natiuitatis fluxit? [illegible]
image-002.jpg L6: tota [illegible] euanuit [illegible] filiu(m)? mirabile(m)?
image-002.jpg L7: diuinitatis? quod [illegible]

Separation of marked passage: red underlining begins beneath “O inestimabilis dilectio ca” in L2 and continues below L3. L2's preceding words and L4 onward are surrounding prose, not included automatically in the quotation. In L3 the visible letter group after seruū looks like redimeret; I have not regularized it. The apparent struck-through group early in L5 is reported as illegible rather than silently removed.

Sample B — image-002.jpg, right, lower paragraph and continuation
image-002.jpg R17: Illa contricio est [illegible] veteru(m)? [illegible]
image-002.jpg R18: Q(uando)? homo dolet de peccato suo et p(ro)p(ter) honore(m)
image-002.jpg R19: dei [illegible; hole] [illegible] se offendisse [illegible]
image-002.jpg R20: sacerdos? hunc mortal[e]? [illegible] p(ro)positu(m) [illegible]
image-002.jpg R21: si sacerdos [illegible] dei et [illegible] ecclesie
image-002.jpg R22: [illegible] p(ro)pter illud ad [illegible] confessione(m)
image-002.jpg R23: habebit et [illegible] in q(uan)tu(m)? ad dei [illegible]
image-002.jpg R24: [illegible] ad rubore(m) [illegible] policione(m)? de
image-002.jpg R25: mali? illa est bona contricio De ista co(n)tricio(ne)?
image-002.jpg R26: d(icitu)r? [illegible] Magna est velud? mare [illegible]
image-002.jpg R27: tua Istam contricione(m) habuit maria magdalē
image-002.jpg R28: et beatus petrus [illegible; lower crop edge]

R17–R28 are prose in one hand with a new paragraph mark within R25. They are not underlined in red like Sample A. The overlapping detail crop was used to check R17 onward, not to create another sample. The words after “homo dolet” in R18 and the “Istam contricionem habuit” sequence in R27 are appreciably clearer than their surrounding lines. Several abbreviated endings remain provisional.

Transforms
Both entire images inspected. image-002 is 5000×4048 pixels. Native, unfiltered crops of image-002: (400,364)–(2250,1092), (2700,1497)–(4650,2347), and (2730,2020)–(4640,3110). No rotation, enhancement or reconstruction. Last two overlap; repeated lines counted only once.

Uncertainty and unread areas
Much of image-001 and image-002's middle-left and upper-right prose is untranscribed. Staining and holes obscure words even in the clearer samples. Baseline counts in these selected areas are reasonably stable, but should still be checked. This is a partial unverified reading; no missing text or citation has been supplied from a likely source. A higher-contrast original photograph or specialist second reading could improve the incomplete connective lines.
